description: Limitation pin (016 T014r, plan D11 as amended after round 9; round-9 review F1, d01). A door through the tracker's own modelled rule: <div><script> is a tag line that opens a script element, so the tracker takes </script> as its end (true for the browser) and the line's blank-ending block resumes after it. CommonMark has only a div block that ends at the first blank line, then starts a processing-instruction block at <?y that runs to ?>. The tracker ignores that start inside its script span; at </script> it resumes the div, the blank line clears it, and x <!--, still a line of CommonMark's PI block, is read as inline text with no closer before the blank line and disarmed; the marker is harvested and the digest that carries only the visible rule is read as stale. Both renderers (markdown-it, commonmark.js) hide the marker in a real comment, as the parent e10da18 does. This is FR-003's exception as amended after round 9 (a long-end span the tracker holds and CommonMark does not). If the mechanism is ever modelled, the digest check passes, so this case fails and must be retired or turned into a guard.
